pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' asserts all existing rows are 0 and that 2 is rejected.
'AC-2' test asserts exactly ['First item','★ Second item','Third item'].
'AC-3' stars 3 and 1 and asserts the starred view lists them in id order with status 200.
'AC-4' checks / and /?show=all both give the full list in id order.

Implemented in src/index.js. The 'AC-5' test asserts both exact links and would fail if either were wrong. The spec line was edited after the go to read 'verified by review: checked by hand', which is not a real step. The test is the real evidence. See the high finding on the edit.
'AC-6' tests Starred, none, empty and __proto__ and asserts 400 with no <li>. src/index.js guards with Object.hasOwn.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'; the 'AC-7' test asserts it. Also checked that traffic/src/index.js fetches the path with its query intact.

findings.what: Commit 48aba10 ('Follow-up edits', github-actions[bot]) edited AC-5 after the go (2026-10-12) with no decision in the spec recording the owner's call and date. The edit also garbled the sentence: the '— verified by review: checked by hand' text now sits mid-sentence, before 'starred list.'. 'Checked by hand' is not a followable review step. The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', which is false.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-5 edit, so the item stays test-proven by 'AC-5: each view links to the other'. If the owner really changed it, record that as a dated decision. Correct the PR's 'Changed after the go' line either way.

findings.what: The PR body says 'Changed after the go: nothing'. The final commit edits an acceptance item in the spec after the go.
findings.fix: State the AC-5 edit under 'Changed after the go', or revert it.

findings.what: The AC-6 test sends '?show=' (empty value) and expects 400. This matches the spec's 'any other value'. No test covers repeated or other-case params such as show=starred&show=all, which the code resolves to the first value.
findings.fix: Optionally add a test for the repeated-param behaviour.

lenses.note: The spec exists with a go. Decisions are followed: starred items keep their id order, and the view is a GET query parameter.

All four state-table rows have tests. AC-5 was edited after the go (high finding). Beyond the ask, the diff also changes traffic-config-check.mjs and the traffic fake app. That is needed for AC-7 and the PR discloses it.

Every AC and state has a test that asserts behaviour. Vitest cannot be run here (not an allowed command), so test results are left to CI. The traffic fake-app change only adds the query to the recorded path.
The README mentions ?show=starred. The 400 behaviour on other values is not documented there, which is minor.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, which guards against __proto__. The SQL uses fixed fragments. Nothing wrong found.
Titles are HTML-escaped, the query value never reaches SQL or HTML, and no planted instructions were found. The spec edit in 48aba10 is flagged under spec.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no stylesheets or UI components. It is checked only through the content asserted in the tests.
No browser was available and there are no UI-flow files beyond the plain HTML page. Page content is covered by tests.
The title is within 72 characters. The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false (see findings).
